charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding Co., Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding Co., Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding Co., Ltd.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding Co., Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding Co., Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding Co., Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding Co., Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding Co., Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue & gross margin mix
segmentRevenue.content:
Shanghai Pharmaceuticals runs three segments at very different economics: Distribution (pharma/device wholesale, SPD logistics, import agency), Manufacturing (branded generics, traditional Chinese medicine, devices) and a small Retail pharmacy chain.

For Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding Co., Ltd.: FY2025 revenue was ~91% Distribution at only 5.79% gross margin, ~8.6% Manufacturing at 57.13% gross margin, and ~3.1% Retail at 11.38% gross margin. Because Manufacturing's margin is roughly 10x Distribution's, a small shift in revenue mix toward Manufacturing moves consolidated gross profit disproportionately more than consolidated revenue -- the central lever in this thesis. Manufacturing and Retail segment revenue, and all three segment gross margins, are disclosed only in the annual report (not every interim), so they are not yet a chartable CSV time series; the figures above and in the KPI cards are the latest (FY2025) disclosure.

What to watch:

  • Distribution gross margin direction (was 5.94% FY2024 to 5.79% FY2025, i.e. still compressing)
  • Whether Manufacturing and Retail revenue grow faster than Distribution (H1 2026: Manufacturing +8.44% YoY vs Distribution +3.75% YoY)
  • Faster-growing sub-segments (import agency, innovative-drug commercialization, overseas sales) gradually shifting the mix within Distribution itself

rndMinority.title: R&D expense & minority interest profit
rndMinority.content:
R&D expense is spend on the Manufacturing segment's drug and device pipeline. Minority interest profit is the share of consolidated net income attributable to non-controlling shareholders in partly-owned subsidiaries -- it never reaches parent-company (and therefore per-share) earnings.

For Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding Co., Ltd.: minority interest profit has run roughly RMB1.2-1.4bn a year, around a fifth of consolidated net income, reflecting the many joint-venture and partly-owned subsidiary structures across Distribution and Manufacturing -- EPS already nets this out, but it is worth watching separately since it is not a lever management fully controls.

What to watch:

  • R&D expense growth versus Manufacturing segment revenue growth (reinvestment intensity)
  • Minority interest profit growing faster than net income (a rising minority share would mean less of future profit growth accrues to parent shareholders)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding Co., Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding Co., Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
